review.method: Independent source comparison of all 80 target entries plus eight adjacent context rows. One comparative-meaning correction applied; approved names unchanged.
uncertainties: Row 356 does not identify the equipped Battery statistic or its unit; rating remains generic.
Row 362 Close window reflects the source action, but the actual X-button behavior has not been playtested.
Row 330 reduced landing motion is stated by the source; the actual animation remains unverified.

source_storage: Source text remains on the original disc; bind by inventory ID and SHA-256.

notes.322: Stick materials have higher structural strength; sheets resist special attacks. Preserve this distinction rather than claim that both strengthen all stats equally.
notes.323: The repeated parenthetical pronunciation of the English title is omitted in English. A blank line retains the original newline count.
notes.324: The last three digits of a model number represent clock speed; no unit is stated in the source.
notes.325: The limit is four spare P-Cards, not four cards total. Source fullwidth Latin P-CARD refers to the approved P-Card term.
notes.326: The hybrid battery energy is converted to electricity but used directly as fuel when the Burner fires. No real-world battery chemistry is inferred.
notes.327: Motor power supports agile movement, while low rotation speed limits top speed. Preserve both qualifications.
notes.329: The source describes different action completion times according to the posture-control pattern. Do not imply that the Balancer changes action selection.
notes.330: The source attributes smaller landing motions to higher damping; retain this alongside reduced shock to parts.
notes.332: The source says Soft has higher braking power and Hard has higher wear resistance. Do not reverse these despite ordinary real-world intuitions.
notes.333: Source fullwidth Latin heading misspells RADAR as RADER. Use the approved Radar spelling. Marking range is distinct from enemy-detection range.
notes.338: Melee Combat is distinct from Close Combat in row 339: rows 349 and 352 show that the former bans Main Weapons and Options, while the latter bans only Main Weapons.
notes.340: WMA is preserved as the source's acronym, without an unsupported expansion. Orchestrator notified to research and register the ruleset.
notes.343: Use Melee Combat consistently with row 338; distinguish it from Close Combat in row 344.
notes.345: Western Rules is a ruleset label; adjacent row 348 specifies a first-hit-wins match, without any geographical location reference.
notes.356: The source omits the battery statistic's unit. Battery rating preserves this omission; do not invent capacity units or mass.
notes.358: Control hints in rows 358-400 are space-separated scrolling text with no source newlines. Five ASCII spaces replace each five-fullwidth-space delimiter. L/R and B/Y mean either listed button, while A+directions, L+Left/Right and R+Left/Right retain explicit combinations.
notes.362: Erase window is translated as Close window; verify the X action during UI playtesting.
notes.366: A+directions selects a range. L undoes and R redoes; do not swap them.
notes.367: The source uses a semicolon after A; normalize it to the same colon separator as adjacent control hints.
notes.372: Releasing A confirms the selected range; X switches scale. Preserve the release action rather than translate it as pressing A.
notes.374: A confirms a character, while Start confirms the complete name. B cancels renaming; X deletes one character.
notes.375: Program card denotes the program-storage card described in row 325. Use approved P-Card rather than introduce a second English card name.
notes.376: A toggles tournament entry registration/removal. The source does not say MARCS for the return destination here; retain generic menu.
notes.380: The setting being adjusted is omitted in the source. Retain generic Adjust pending the active settings screen.
notes.383: The action category being selected is not specified in the source. Retain generic action rather than invent attack or movement.
notes.388: The item or system ending is omitted in the source. Generic shutdown status preserves that omission.
notes.392: The source return destination is generic menu here, not expressly MARCS.
notes.398: The selection object is omitted in source rows 398-400. Retain generic Select. B means Back in 398/399 but Cancel in 400.

translations:
Option
Additional equipment such as bombs,
shields and expansion batteries.

Material
Used to strengthen a Marionette's
frame and Armor.
Stick materials offer high strength,
while sheets resist
special attacks.

Maintenance Kit

Includes grease to keep moving
parts running smoothly, and
Repair Kits for damaged parts.
Perform regular maintenance
to keep your Marionette's
performance from declining.

CPU
Interprets the program and sends
commands to each part.
The last three model-number digits
indicate clock speed.
If you want to create complex
programs, choose a CPU with
the highest performance you can.

P-Card
A card for storing programs.
Larger-capacity cards can store
a greater number of
Program Chips.
Regulations allow you to carry
no more than four spare cards!

Battery
A hybrid battery that supplies
a Marionette's energy.
Its energy is converted to electricity,
but is used directly as fuel when
the Burner fires. If you use
the Burner often, choose a Battery
with high combustion efficiency.

Motor
The main Motor that powers
a Marionette.
The number in its model name
indicates Motor power.
More power enables more agile movement,
but low rotation speed
reduces top speed.

Burner
A Burner Set used for jumping,
acceleration and deceleration.
There are various types emphasizing
jumping, acceleration/deceleration
or fuel economy.
Choose one that suits
your tactics.

Balancer
Memory containing a Marionette's
posture-control patterns.
These patterns affect how long
each action takes to complete.
Choose one to suit the actions
you want to prioritize.

Damper
Absorbs shocks
to the legs.
Greater rebound force
enables more agile movements.
Greater damping absorbs
shock to the parts and reduces
the motions needed for landings.

Dash Gear
A device for dash movement.
A lower gear ratio
provides a higher top speed.
A higher gear ratio lowers
top speed but reduces
the time needed to reach it.

Brake
A gas brake for slowing down
during dash movement.
Three types are available:
Soft, Intermediate and Hard.
Soft offers high braking power;
Hard offers high wear resistance.

Radar
Detects enemies,
obstacles and other objects.
A wider enemy-detection range
makes enemies easier to find.
However, a narrow marking range
makes it harder to hit enemies,
so keep this in mind.

Armor
Protective plating against
enemy attacks.
You must purchase Armor
that fits the Marionette
you will use.
Select that Marionette
before making your purchase.

Official Rules
Time limit: 180 seconds.
The match ends when either
Marionette runs out of hit points.

WMA Rules
Time limit: 180 seconds.
The match ends when either
Marionette runs out of energy.

Western Rules
Time limit: 60 seconds.
The first to land an attack wins.

Melee Combat
Time limit: 180 seconds.
Main Weapons and Options
are prohibited.

Ground Combat
Time limit: 180 seconds.
Jumping is prohibited.

Aerial Combat
Time limit: 180 seconds.
You take damage while on the ground.

Close Combat
Time limit: 180 seconds.
Main Weapons are prohibited.

Endurance Battle
Time limit: 300 seconds.

Lightweight Tournament
Time limit: 180 seconds.
Only Marionettes weighing
12,000 g or less may enter.

Heavyweight Tournament
Time limit: 180 seconds.
Only Marionettes weighing
15,000 g or more may enter.

Energy-Saving Tournament
Only Marionettes with
an equipped Battery rating of
3,000 or less may enter.

Championship
Time limit: 180 seconds.
Official Rules.
